Installation on Windows systems
The official releases of PHP on Windows are recommended for production use, but PHP can also be built from source.
PHP can also be installed on Azure App Services (aka Microsoft Azure, Windows Azure, or (Windows) Azure Web Apps).
The Installation section of the frequently asked questions covers common installation and configuration issues that may be encountered.
Optional local development provisioning preview
An experimental Microsoft DevConfig PHP provisioning preview is available in a personal fork. This is not an official PHP recommendation or a Microsoft-signed release. Its PHP workload installs PowerShell 7, the Visual C++ Redistributable, and PHP; it does not install Composer, IIS, Apache, or frameworks.
Review the guide, source, and package terms before running it on a disposable Windows development VM. Installers may request elevation. From the root of the reviewed personal-fork checkout, run:
.\src\Workloads\install-source.ps1 -Workload php
This runs unsigned development source and installs software; it is not a dry run. Follow the guide's prerequisites and execution-policy requirements. Use the official downloads and manual installation instructions below for production and web server setup.
